FDA review cycle verified: MR-141/phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% presbyopia sNDA, PDUFA 2026-10-17. VEGA-3 randomized double-masked placebo-controlled Phase 3 (n=545) met primary endpoint: 27.2% vs 11.5%, p<0.0001; key secondary Day 1 endpoint p=0.0002; no treatment-related serious adverse events and no new safety signal. FDA NDA/priority-review cycle verified for chronic hepatitis B with PDUFA 2026-10-26; Breakthrough and Fast Track designations reported. B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials met the primary endpoint; pooled functional cure 19% (233/1220) vs 0/614, p<0.001 in both trials; 26% vs 0% in lower-HBsAg subgroup. Safety was acceptable but not trivial: pooled on-treatment AEs 89% vs 65% placebo, serious AEs 4% vs 1%, treatment-related serious AEs 2%; discontinuation about 3%. As of 2026-10-06 no earlier U.S. FDA final action was identified. Sources: https://www.gsk.com/en-gb/media/press-releases/bepirovirsen-achieves-unprecedented-functional-cure-rates-with-potential-to-redefine-treatment-for-chronic-hepatitis-b/ ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1131399/000165495426003977/a1144c.htm

BLA accepted for accelerated-approval review, PDUFA 2026-10-30; FDA denied requested Priority Review and initially questioned whether accelerated-approval eligibility was adequately justified. RRP-001 was Phase 1/2, single-arm, n=32: 81.3% reduced surgeries, 28.1% required no surgery during the following year; median decrease 3 surgeries with 95% CI 2-3; all treatment-related AEs were grade 1-2, no treatment-related SAEs. By August 2026 INOVIO reported late-cycle review completed and all scheduled pre-licensure inspections completed; FDA did not discuss the earlier accelerated-approval concern at an informal clinical meeting, but no public final inspection/CMC outcome was disclosed. As of 2026-10-06 no earlier FDA final action was identified. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1055726/000105572626000024/ino-63026x8kex991.htm ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-56729-6

sNDA for accelerated approval in sickle cell disease accepted with Priority Review; PDUFA 2026-11-01; confirmatory REIGNITE Phase 3 initiated. RISE UP Phase 3 randomized 207 patients. Hemoglobin-response primary endpoint strongly positive: 40.6% vs 2.9%, p<0.0001. Hemoglobin and indirect-bilirubin key secondary endpoints also p<0.0001. However, the annualized sickle-cell pain-crisis co-primary endpoint did not reach significance (2.62 vs 3.05; p=0.1213), and PROMIS Fatigue key secondary endpoint was not met (p=0.7112). Safety was reported consistent with prior mitapivat experience. As of 2026-10-06 no earlier FDA final action was identified. Sources: https://investor.agios.com/news-releases/news-release-details/agios-announces-topline-results-rise-phase-3-trial-mitapivat ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1439222/000143922226000118/agio-20260630.htm

FDA accepted MYQORZO aficamten sNDA to add MAPLE-HCM data; PDUFA 2026-11-14. MAPLE-HCM randomized double-blind active-comparator Phase 3: pVO2 LSM difference 2.3 mL/kg/min, 95% CI 1.5-3.1, p<0.0001; 5/6 secondary endpoints favored aficamten. Existing U.S.-approved MYQORZO carries heart-failure risk/REMS, so safety remains important. PFS, one of two primary endpoints, was statistically significant; primary OS analysis showed HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.62-1.01), p=0.057 and did not meet statistical significance. Later follow-up was directionally favorable but nominal. Mixed co-primary architecture keeps V3.2 Stats Gate at REVIEW. Vanda BLA for imsidolimab in GPP accepted with PDUFA 2026-12-12. GEMINI-1 randomized 45 patients; 53% on each imsidolimab dose were clear/almost clear at Week 4 vs 13% placebo (p=0.023 for each comparison). GEMINI-2 supported maintenance and no serious adverse events led to discontinuation. Anaptys retains a financial collaboration exposure; Vanda is the U.S. applicant. Relacorilant is a resubmission after FDA's 2025 CRL stated additional evidence of effectiveness was required. FDA requested additional analyses in April 2026; Corcept resubmitted the same NDA data package with those analyses on June 17 and received PDUFA 2026-12-17. Prior effectiveness deficiency remains a major regulatory risk until FDA accepts the remediation. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1088856/000162828026050613/cort-20260630.htm

Launch-HTN Phase 3 (n=1,083) met primary endpoint with 9.1 mmHg placebo-adjusted SBP reduction at Week 6, p<0.0001; Advance-HTN pivotal trial independently met 24-hour SBP primary endpoint, p=0.001. Safety was generally favorable with monitorable hyperkalemia risk. Relutrigine NDA accepted for Priority Review; PDUFA extended to 2026-12-27 after additional sensitivity analyses were deemed a major amendment. EMBOLD registrational cohort stopped early for efficacy: 53% placebo-adjusted seizure reduction over 16 weeks (p<0.0002), 66% increase in motor seizure-free days (p=0.034), no drug-related SAEs. FDA reported no major safety or efficacy concerns at mid-cycle and no AdCom planned, but the sensitivity-analysis amendment keeps missing-data/statistical robustness at REVIEW. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954826000083/prax-20260630.htm ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954826000069/prax-20260629.htm ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954825000114/prax-20251204.htm

Two randomized double-blind pivotal Phase 3 studies in herniorrhaphy and bunionectomy both met all primary and secondary endpoints; SPID0-48 improvement vs placebo was highly significant in both (p<0.001) with reduced opioid use and generally placebo-comparable TEAEs. FDA accepted ANKTIVA+BCG sBLA for BCG-unresponsive papillary-only NMIBC; PDUFA 2027-01-06. QUILT-3.032 Cohort B was open-label/single-arm (n=80): 12-month DFS 58.2% (95% CI 46.6-68.2), 36-month PFS 83.1%, durable cystectomy avoidance, and low high-grade treatment-related toxicity. ANKTIVA is already FDA-approved with BCG for CIS ± papillary disease; this is a label-expansion review. Sources: https://ir.immunitybio.com/news-releases/news-release-details/immunitybio-announces-fda-acceptance-supplemental-bla-anktivar ; https://ir.immunitybio.com/news-releases/news-release-details/anktivar-bcg-demonstrates-96-survival-bladder-cancer-three-years

FDA accepted z-rostudirsen BLA with Priority Review; PDUFA 2027-01-21, Accelerated Approval sought on dystrophin surrogate. DELIVER REC (n=32) met primary endpoint: muscle-content-adjusted dystrophin 5.46% of normal at 6 months, p<0.0001, a 7-fold increase; functional improvement was observed across six prespecified measures, with two nominal p<0.05. Confirmatory randomized Phase 3 FORZETTO has started and FDA aligned on its design. Safety was favorable overall, but surrogate-based approval keeps regulatory/benefit-risk uncertainty material. Sources: https://investors.dyne-tx.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dyne-therapeutics-announces-us-fda-acceptance-biologics-license/ ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818794/000119312526084207/dyn-ex99_1.htm

Essential3 Study 1 randomized placebo-controlled primary mADL11 p<0.0001 with all key secondaries significant; Study 2 randomized withdrawal primary p=0.0369. Prespecified missing-data tipping-point analysis remained significant at maximum tested shift (p=0.0026). FDA mid-cycle identified no major safety/efficacy concerns; BIMO inspections completed with no Form FDA 483 observations. FDA accepted ZORYVE roflumilast cream 0.05% sNDA to extend mild-moderate AD indication to infants 3-24 months; PDUFA 2027-02-23. INTEGUMENT-INFANT was open-label n=101: 58% achieved EASI-75 at Week 4; 34.4% of completers achieved vIGA-AD success; no serious AEs, one AE discontinuation, and no new safety signal. Submission also includes infant Phase 1 PK. FDA accepted zipalertinib NDA for previously treated EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC; PDUFA 2027-02-27. REZILIENT1 phase I/II open-label efficacy population n=176: confirmed ORR 35.2% (95% CI 28.2-42.8), median DOR 8.8 months; prior platinum without ex20ins-targeted therapy ORR 40.0%. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs included anemia 7%, pneumonitis/rash 2.5% each. Sources: https://www.taiho.co.jp/en/release/2026/20260428_1.html ; https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO-25-00763

FDA accepted zanzalintinib + atezolizumab NDA for previously treated metastatic CRC; verified PDUFA is 2026-12-03. STELLAR-303 met one dual primary endpoint in ITT OS: HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.69-0.93), p=0.0045. The other dual primary endpoint, OS in the non-liver-metastases subgroup, did not reach significance at final analysis: HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.66-1.05), p=0.1185. Mixed dual-primary result keeps statistics gate REVIEW. Sources: https://ir.exelixis.com/news-releases/news-release-details/exelixis-announces-us-fda-accepted-new-drug-application ; https://ir.exelixis.com/news-releases/news-release-details/exelixis-provides-update-phase-3-stellar-303-trial-evaluating

FDA accepted lonvo-z BLA with Priority Review; PDUFA 2027-03-10 and no AdCom currently planned. HAELO randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 3 (n=80) showed 87% lower monthly attack rate vs placebo, p<0.0001; all key secondary endpoints significant, with no serious or grade >=3 AEs in lonvo-z arm in the published analysis. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652130/000119312526385194/ntla-ex99_1.htm ; https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2600931

Pivotal bioequivalence study showed pitolisant GR 17.8 mg bioequivalent to WAKIX: AUC ratio 108.46% (90% CI 103.74-113.41) and Cmax ratio 99.65% (90% CI 91.95-108.00), within conventional BE bounds; dosing-optimization study supported starting directly at 17.8 mg and reported no new safety/tolerability issues. FDA accepted varegacestat NDA; PDUFA 2027-04-28. RINGSIDE randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 3 met PFS primary endpoint HR 0.16 (95% CI 0.071-0.375), p<0.0001 and all key secondary endpoints including ORR 56% vs 9%; manageable class-consistent safety. Sources: https://investors.immunome.com/immunome-announces-u-s-fda-acceptance-of-new-drug-application-for-varegacestat-for-the-treatment-of-adults-with-desmoid-tumors/ ; https://investors.immunome.com/immunome-announces-positive-topline-results-from-phase-3-ringside-trial-of-varegacestat-in-patients-with-desmoid-tumors/

FDA accepted AXS-12 NDA for cataplexy in narcolepsy; PDUFA 2027-05-01. SYMPHONY randomized double-blind Phase 3 met primary endpoint: weekly cataplexy attacks reduced 83% vs 66% placebo, rate ratio 0.49, p=0.018; multiple supportive symptom endpoints favored AXS-12. ENCORE randomized-withdrawal Phase 3 independently met its primary endpoint (p=0.017) and supported durability; no new safety signal. INDIGO Phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trial met primary endpoint with 56% reduction in flare risk, HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.277-0.711), p=0.0005; well tolerated. PEAK randomized Phase 3 met primary PFS endpoint: median 16.5 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.39-0.65), p<0.0001 against active comparator sunitinib; no unique combination safety risk reported. FDA accepted Priority Review sNDA for lower Joenja doses in children age 4+ weighing 13-27 kg; PDUFA 2027-01-30. Same product was FDA-approved in Sept 2026 for children 4-11 weighing >=27 kg after prior pediatric CRL remediation. Current lower-weight submission is supported by positive pediatric Phase 3 findings plus additional scientific/clinical-pharmacology assessments supporting dosing. Existing approval strengthens safety/clinical context, but lower-weight exposure/dose adequacy remains the key review question and CMC for any new strength is not assumed resolved. Global randomized double-masked placebo-controlled Phase 3 DRAGON (n=104) met primary endpoint with 35.7% reduction in annualized lesion growth vs placebo, p=0.0033; key secondary DAF lesion growth also significant and treatment was well tolerated. Applications also cite published real-world evidence and favorable safety. Under fixed FDA-V3.2 rules, an explicit failed confirmatory primary endpoint is a statistics hard-gate FAIL. FDA accepted ozekibart (INBRX-109) BLA for unresectable/metastatic conventional chondrosarcoma; PDUFA 2027-04-14 and no filing review issues identified at acceptance. Randomized ChonDRAgon registrational trial met primary PFS endpoint: HR 0.479 (95% CI 0.33-0.68), p<0.0001; median PFS 5.52 vs 2.66 months, with disease control rate 54% vs 27.5%. FDA accepted deucrictibant immediate-release NDA for on-demand HAE attacks; PDUFA 2027-04-23. RAPIDe-3 pivotal Phase 3 met primary and all 11 secondary efficacy endpoints. Median time to onset of symptom relief was 1.28 hours vs >12 hours placebo (p<0.0001); complete symptom resolution 11.95 hours vs >24 hours (p<0.0001). No treatment-related serious AEs or TEAE discontinuations were reported.
